narrative: Material PL1__MF685688 exhibits smooth, near-continuous demand averaging 1,151 units/day with a CV of 0.469 and a statistically significant upward trend (p=0.0077). Lead times are moderate in variability (CV=0.465, mean=2.55 days), with transport as the dominant uncertainty source. The (r,Q) EOQ policy is optimal: it reduces orders from 289 to 43 per year, cuts total annual costs by 60.6%, and raises safety stock to 2,659 units to achieve the 95% service level. The storage capacity constraint is respected with 99% utilisation post-replenishment.
warnings: Storage capacity nearly fully utilised: safety_stock (2659) + order_quantity (6628) = 9287, which is 99.0% of max_storage_units (9380.314).
Upward demand trend detected — policy should be reviewed within 6 months as growing demand may exhaust storage capacity.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and near-continuous (non-zero fraction 98.3%, CV 0.469) with moderate lead-time variability. A fixed-reorder-point, fixed-order-quantity policy optimally balances ordering and holding costs. The EOQ formula analytically minimises total annual cost given the known unit cost, holding rate, and ordering cost.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage constraint is nearly binding: combined safety stock and order quantity consume 99.0% of available storage. The detected upward demand trend will increase both required safety stock and reorder frequency over time. A capacity expansion review is recommended within 6 months.
